_comment: Kelp Watch analysis polygons per docs/03. One Feature per area the analysis compares kelp over. Each declares polygon_id (the key every kelp and comparison row joins on), purpose (near_site, control or regional), site_ids (the stations this polygon is compared against, so no analysis code string-matches a polygon name), and source_file -- the Kelp Watch export its rows arrive in, because the CSV names the geometry it describes nowhere in the file (docs/02). kelp_watch pins the dataset revision the exports came from; bumping it obsoletes every landing at the old revision, because a newer revision may revise history as well as extend it. Geometry is WGS84 (RFC 7946) and is now recorded for all six, as a RECONSTRUCTION rather than a recovered original. Kelp Watch has no named-bed catalogue -- area selection there is draw-on-map or upload-a-file -- so the outlines the operator drew exist in no upstream list and cannot be fetched back. What is recorded instead is derived from Kelp Watch's own classified-cell vector tiles (docs/02, 'The cells behind the export'): every bed is a spatially isolated cluster of 30 m cells, and each outline is that cluster's historic footprint dilated by 90 m and simplified to 40 m. That is not an eyeballed shape -- it selects exactly the cells its landed export was summed over and no others, with at least 49 m of margin inside and 537 m of clearance to the nearest cell of any other bed. Checked against the public /aggregate endpoint on 2026-08-30, all six: count_cells_historic_footprint matches the recorded value and the whole 213-line response diffs clean against the landed CSV, zero differing lines. Nothing in the pipeline computes from these outlines -- the export arrives already summed over the selected geometry -- but docs/04 s4.5's distance-decay test needs them, and that is the stage that should refuse a polygon without one.
_provisional: The pairing and purpose rule, applied here rather than by eye (https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/86). PURPOSE is decided by containment and needs no threshold: near_site is a bed containing a project sensor, control is one that does not. Measured against these outlines the nearest project sensor is 0 m for KELP:LA-JOLLA and 9791 m for the next bed, so there is no number to tune. regional is RESERVED and carried by nothing: docs/03 defines it by extent -- a bed representing a wider province rather than a site -- and all six beds here are local, running 0.44 to 18.20 km2. Whether the project gains beds that earn it is https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/96, which is why the value is kept rather than deleted; deleting it would decide that PRD. Until 9220aef this file said KELP:LA-JOLLA was regional because NDBC:LJAC1 sits inside it. The recorded outline puts that station 1731 m outside, to the north, as SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER is at 1718 m, because Scripps Pier is north of the La Jolla kelp forest. That premise is what issue 86 was opened about and it is now gone. SITE_IDS has four legs and is the union of them. (a) Both project sensors pair with every bed: docs/04 s4.5 is a distance-decay test, so the far beds are the measurement rather than noise in it, and dropping them would delete the ladder. (b) Every public station within 8 km of the bed that has an ingested record. 8 km is not tuned -- every bed's nearest public stations sit at or below 5625 m and the next is at or above 8369 m, so any threshold in (5.6 km, 8.4 km) gives these same pairings. (c) The public references able to supply a climatology, which today are NDBC:LJAC1 and SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER and no others. Leg (c) is why those two stay on all six beds: NDBC:46266 is nearer to three of them but its record begins 2019-12 and carries no anomaly at all under docs/04 s3, so pairing by distance alone would have replaced 178 anomaly-bearing quarters with none. Nearest is not the same as most useful. (d) The site derived from this bed, if there is one. A derived site (docs/03) has no instrument: it carries a reduction of a spatially continuous product over one bed's outline, so it pairs with that bed and with no other, and it is never paired by distance -- legs (b) and (c) do not apply to it and the 8 km radius is a fact about measured stations only. WHAT LEG (d) ADDED: the six MUR L4 SST beds SST:LA-JOLLA, SST:DEL-MAR, SST:SOLANA-BEACH, SST:ENCINITAS, SST:SAN-DIEGO and SST:IMPERIAL-BEACH, one per bed, supplying the satellite leg of the docs/04 s4.5 three-way comparison that had never been built (https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/106). It is the only leg that reaches all six beds with a series measured at the bed rather than borrowed from up the coast: KELP:SAN-DIEGO and KELP:IMPERIAL-BEACH keep La Jolla references 13535 m and 32313 m away under legs (b) and (c), and their SST is over the bed itself. The leg covers every bed or none -- a bed without one while others have one would make its coverage a property of which beds someone got round to, and s4.5 would read the hole as a spatial finding. WHAT LEG (b) ADDED: NDBC:46254 to KELP:LA-JOLLA at 1396 m, nearer than either reference that bed already had, and NDBC:46266 to KELP:DEL-MAR at 0 m -- inside the outline, so not a neighbour in the docs/04 s1 sense but a measurement of the water that canopy is in -- and to KELP:SOLANA-BEACH at 2331 m and KELP:ENCINITAS at 5625 m. Nothing was removed. WHAT LEG (b) DID NOT ADD, and the gate that would. SDRTOMS:PLOO is 5264 m from KELP:SAN-DIEGO and SDRTOMS:SBOO is 2968 m from KELP:IMPERIAL-BEACH -- the nearest sites of any kind to those two beds -- and both are held out for want of a record, not for want of range. PLOO has no ingested rows at all (https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/63); SBOO has 2023-06-29 to 2023-12-31. Neither can be validated either: the nearest site to either mooring is the other, 20.2 km away, and everything else is 21 to 48 km, so there is no reference in range to compare against. Both moorings do carry a 1.0 m bin, which is depth-legal against NDBC:46254 and NDBC:46266 at 0.46 m, SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER at 0.5 m and NDBC:LJAC1 at 3.4 m, so the comparison is available whenever a reference appears. THE GATE: a station within 8 km joins a bed's site_ids when it has a record overlapping the kelp series and has been shown to track regional forcing -- correlation against the network, the same reasoning features/validation.py already uses to report correlation across a depth gap while refusing bias. Until then KELP:SAN-DIEGO and KELP:IMPERIAL-BEACH keep the La Jolla references at 13535 m and 32313 m, which is a weak docs/04 s4.5 comparison and is recorded as such rather than hidden. COOPS:9410230 is within 8 km of KELP:LA-JOLLA and is also held out for want of a record: it has no ingested rows. It is the same NOS platform as NDBC:LJAC1 and 14.4 m from SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER, so when its water level does land, whether one platform may contribute two references is https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/69 and must be answered before it is paired. SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER is paired at both sensor depths, 0.5 m and 5.0 m, rather than at one chosen here: they are independent series with independent coverage bookkeeping, docs/04 s4.1 is exploratory by decision, and whether a surface and a 5 m shore record behave differently against canopy is a question the screen answers rather than one to settle by assertion. Widening the pool widens the docs/04 s5 denominator, which is accepted and is https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/81. Changing any of this is a data(registry) edit needing no code.

kelp_watch._comment: From the export's own recommended-citation download, retrieved 2026-08-26: Bell, T., K. Cavanaugh, D. Siegel. 2024. SBC LTER: Time series of quarterly NetCDF files of kelp biomass in the canopy from Landsat 5, 7 and 8, since 1984 (ongoing) ver 23. Environmental Data Initiative.

properties.name: La Jolla kelp bed
properties._verified: Reconstructed outline, verified 2026-08-30: encloses all 8309 cells of this bed's historic footprint and no cell of any other bed, whose nearest is 6239 m away. Queried against kelpwatch.org's /aggregate endpoint it returns count_cells_historic_footprint = 8309, matching kelp_lajolla.csv, and all 213 lines of the response are identical to that landed file.
properties.notes: The bed both project sensors sit in, which is what makes it near_site under the rule in _provisional -- containment, computed rather than taken from the deployment record. PROJ:TIDBIT-1 and PROJ:TIDBIT-2 both fall inside this outline; the nearest project sensor to any other bed is 9791 m away. Its nearest public station is NDBC:46254 at 1396 m, added by leg (b) of the rule and nearer than either reference this bed previously had: NDBC:LJAC1 sits 1731 m north of it and SIO:LAJOLLA-PIER 1718 m, because Scripps Pier is north of the La Jolla kelp forest. Until 9220aef this note opened by calling it the bed containing NDBC:LJAC1, which the recorded outlines falsified; that is what https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/86 was opened about and it is now settled.

properties.notes: The smallest bed exported. Genuinely empty for most of the record, which makes it the bed where a fabricated cloud-gap zero would be least visible (docs/02). SCCOOS:DELMAR paired 2026-09-02 under leg (b) at 4546 m: NDBC:46266 is nearer but begins 2019-12 and clears no baseline, so until now this bed had no local series that could carry an anomaly at all (docs/04 s4.5). Only the mooring's 1 m series clears the 2007-2019 window; its 15 m series is null pending https://github.com/cweber12/kelp-compare/issues/147.
